title: New / Returning Players Guide to Warcraft III
excerpt: Where to start with Warcraft III today: what you need to play, how to learn the basics, the community ladder, build orders, tools, who to watch and where to compete.

children.text: Welcome (back) to Warcraft III! Despite Blizzard taking away some key features from the real-time strategy game we all grew to love over the past 15-20 years, the community is still keeping the game afloat and strong. The following sections in this new / returning players guide for Warcraft III will point you towards resources and communities that will help you get into the game no matter what skill level you are at.
Do I need to buy Reforged to play Warcraft III?
You DON’T need Reforged to play Warcraft III
A Reign of Chaos key is enough
As you may have heard, Reforged was a disaster. One of the more frequently asked questions is: do I need to buy Reforged to play Warcraft III? The answer is

If you had your classic Warcraft III keys (Reign of Chaos and The Frozen Throne) assigned to a Battle.net account (required sometime around 2010 and after). If you have them assigned to your account, you will still have to download the Reforged client to play the game. If you do not have Reforged purchased on your account, you will still be able play but just without having access to load Reforged graphics.

However, if you did not originally purchase classic Warcraft III, you will need to purchase Reforged to play Warcraft III. Good to know that even if you have Reforged, you can still choose play on with the classic graphics. It’s what most people do and is essentially the same game we all know and love.
The best way to learn the basics of the game

If you are a new player to the game, the best way to learn is by playing through the campaign. The campaign (besides having a great story) is split into different parts by the different races. It introduces you to the game’s mechanics, the units, the
, the tech trees, hotkeys, and so much more that is basic knowledge to get into the game.

Playing through the campaign will most likely influence what race you like the most and what race you’ll want to compete with, whether it’s what you think looks coolest or what units or heroes feel most fun to play with.
I highly recommend checking out the Re-Reforged campaign made by a community member (InsaneMonster at Hive Workshop), which you can read more about

The recommended route for preparing yourself to be ready to play Warcraft 3 online is
1. Beat the campaign
2. Beat Computer Easy in a custom game. Also focus on a small set of maps to practice, and pick ones that are always in the current competitive map pool such as Last Refuge, Tidehunters, Northern Isles, or Concealed Hill.
3. Beat Computer Normal regularly. Also have at least one beginner’s build learned and in your arsenal by this point.
4. Beat Computer Insane.
5.
How to play against others at your skill level

So you’ve got the hang of the game, got down a build, familiarized yourself with some maps, and you’ve tried your skills versus a computer. You feel ready to play against real people, but where’s the best place to do that online?

While playing custom maps on Battle.net is great, melee Warcraft on there unfortunately sucks. Their ranking system is subpar and they don’t offer many servers so you could suffer from lag depending on the location of your opponent. Blizzard has slowly built up what their built-in ladder BNet has to offer and finally gave us things like ranked ladder and profiles that keep track of your stats. So while BNet is fine and has gotten better in recent years, there’s still some bugs, lack of servers, not ideal matchmaking, and there’s still a lot left to be desired.
W3Champions is the ladder made by and for the community. It adds many new and old features to the game, such as:
Ranked ladder from newbie to grand master
Fair skill matchups after five placement matches
Improved pings via host bots for interregional play
New interface in the old style
Watch LIVE games (with a 3 minute delay) using FloTV built into the client
Download replays from other players on the W3Champions website

Make sure Battle.net App is open

A few common issues can get solved by ensuring the correct path was used, having your firewall allow W3Champions applications, or simply restarting your computer/the W3Champions applications. If you are having any issues, I recommend you join their
and ask any questions there or check their
that has a few tutorials on how to fix common issues.
W3Champions has profiles that keep track of your lifetime stats, league placements based on your skill level and activity, history of matches, and more!
Improve your skills with strategy guides & build orders
Learn a build order from our
Maybe you’re brand new to the game, or maybe you’ve returned and you have no idea what strategies are good nowadays and you need some build orders and other helpful guides to help you out.
A good starting point would be our very own
. From here, you can navigate to your race and learn different builds, as well as learning general game knowledge such as creep routes by map and race and game mechanics.
Additionally, many resources have been made over the years to help players learn build orders and strategies.
A good place to start is Longjacket’s

, which is an amazing website with multiple tools to help you learn the game and track players throughout the scene. For the purposes of this, I wanted to highlight the build order section which serves as a database of community contributed build orders. Each build order not only tells you the background of each build and the contributor’s thoughts on when and how you should use it, but it lists out in detail each step of the build with corresponding food counts to help you have a guide to follow along with specific markers. There’s also attached replays, notes on when the review was last updated, upvoting, and more.
Here are some other specific build orders & knowledge guides from others in the community. Reach out to us if you feel like we should add any others here or if you feel any are out of date.

Longjacket’s Ape Science WC3 Research Facility

Reimagined maps and missions, detailed and expanded lore, and more!

Keep up with the competitive scene and the Warcraft III community
There’s usually something every day or at least every other day in the Warcraft III scene and below are the best ways to keep up with the best players in the competitive scene.
– Mentioned above as a hub for replays, news, and more, Warcraft3.info also has a calendar that is consistently updated with upcoming and ongoing events.
– Everything you need to know about the competitive scene. Past, ongoing, and upcoming tournaments. Information on players, casters, and prominent members of the community.
– The #1 spot to watch high-level live Warcraft III. They run a
channel that casts the majority of major events, as well as community events. They also have a
that has over 10+ years of Warcraft III commentary videos and more. Asides from following their Twitch and subscribing to their YouTube, you can join their Discord

– A Discord server originally focused on helping new players learn the game, is now a large community of all different skill levels who come together to train and learn. It is also the home of Gym Newbie League.

– A Discord server for the WC3 community ladder mentioned above. This Discord is the first place to get new updates about W3Champions, as well as the best place to ask the developers any questions or issues you may have relating to the ladder.
– French Undead player SyDe’s Discord server. A community hangout to chat about current events, the game, and just general conversation between community members.
– OCE-based team Zero Effort’s Discord server. A community hangout to chat about current events, the game, and just general conversation between community members.
– A Discord server started out of German-based Rocket Beans TV’s WC3 content (a recurring WC3 series called Creepjack and a league called Creepcamp).
Competitive leagues, tournaments and weekly cups you can join

– Gym Newbie League (GNL) is a league created by the Gym discord team with the goal of providing a competitive and fun space for new and veteran players to participate in a team league with solo matches.

– Fountain of Manner League (FOML) is an NA-based solo league for all skill levels with an emphasis on creating as fair as possible matchups for everyone, done by creating groups of 8 players all around the same MMR. There are prizes for all groups.
Creep Camp League by Rocket Beans

– A league started by Rocket Beans open to all skill levels with separate divisions and their own independent point system based on performances within your group. Point systems affect what group you are placed
– Weekly open cup hosted by B2W with a minimum of $50 prize pool. Every Friday @ 1PM ET / 7PM CET
